Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to India's chase. Ben Stokes and his men form a huddle with the skipper providing a brief pep-talk as they spread out to the field. Out walk the two Indian openers, Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul. Chris Woakes has the new ball and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Washington Sundar delivered a standout performance, showcasing his all-round value. After contributing with the bat in the first innings, he rose to the occasion with the ball when England’s resistance started to take shape through the Root-Stokes partnership. Introduced at a critical juncture, Sundar made an immediate impact, capitalizing on the pitch’s assistance to dismiss three key batters, Root, Jamie Smith and Ben Stokes, before wrapping up the innings by outsmarting Bashir. It was a timely and tactical spell that shifted the momentum India’s way. With the spin doing the talk, the pacers too, did their part with Mohammed Siraj and Jasprit Bumrah fishing out two English batters apiece. Strikingly, barring the top three, each English batter was bowled out, which also shows that the Indians just kept targeting the stumps constantly and reaped the rewards on this tiring pitch. Well then, 193 is the magical number for the Indians to register their second consecutive win at Lord's. But the Indian openers will have to face the testing new ball and a rhythmic Jofra Archer who bowled exceptionally well in the first innings. The hosts will expect no less from their premier pacer and will aim to snag a couple of wickets, or even more, to peg India on the back foot. Back in a bit with the run chase. IT IS GAME ON!

England stumbled out of the gates once more as their top-order failed to hold firm, but stability arrived in the form of a 67-run partnership between Joe Root and Ben Stokes. Root’s dismissal, however, proved the turning point. From a promising 154 for 4, England spiraled to 192 all out, with Stokes finishing as the next best contributor on 33. A closer look at the scorecard adds another layer to the story. Extras accounted for 32 runs, a striking figure given the final total. And 25 of those came via byes, further reflecting the chaotic nature of the surface and the challenges faced by both sides.

A job well done by the Indian bowlers overall. They have managed to keep England under 200, a total that not only reflects their bowling discipline but also delivers a psychological boost heading into the all-important chase. Barring Joe Root, the English batting unit appeared visibly unsettled, as none were able to make a meaningful contribution. In fairness, the pitch had turned increasingly treacherous, offering sharp turn and unpredictable bounce that made every run hard-earned and every mistake costly.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the final session of the day. It's been a highly intense contest so far, and expect the action to just double down in this evening stretch. The umpires and players are out in the middle. The sun shines brightly in London as the Indians spread out to the field. Ben Stokes and Chris Woakes are all set to resume their batting post the break. Washington Sundar (7-2-13-2) to bowl from the Nursery End. Here we go...
... DAY 4, THIRD SESSION ...

The breakthroughs eventually came through spin, with Sundar outfoxing Root just as he looked primed for another marathon innings, and soon after removing Jamie Smith off a ripper that ascended the Indian spirits, as England slipped down from 154/4 to 164/6. The onus now lies largely on the skipper, Ben Stokes, and the hosts will expect their tail to wag once again as it did in the first inning. But it is not going to be that easy this time, with the pitch turning into a landmine. England's aim will be to bat through the day and add as many runs as possible. But, how much will they deem enough for taking ten Indian wickets? All will be answered in a very crucial post-Tea session. Join us back in a few minutes' time.

Stokes and Root displayed admirable grit against India’s persistent pace unit, which exploited the pitch’s uneven bounce and sharp lateral movement. Their 67-run stand held value, but it was far from convincing. The ball beat the bat time and again, and Root also survived a tense LBW appeal but was saved by the umpire’s call. Despite their disciplined resistance, India endured frustrating moments as 31 runs leaked through extras, which is the second-best in this English batting line-up after Root. Each was a product of extreme deviation that left the keeper with very little chance.

As the game has deepened, the pitch has fully embraced unpredictability. Cracks have widened considerably, turning each delivery into a potential hazard. Balls either shoot through low or rear up viciously, leaving batters with little choice but to rely on concentration and resilience. The surface has behaved like a minefield, quite literally, unforgiving and increasingly volatile.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 Overs, 77 Runs, 2 Wickets. What a nerve-tickling afternoon session this has been. This match has ebbed and flowed back and forth with none of the two side ready to concede a single inch. And as has been the case since this Test commenced, just when a team gains momentum, the other bounces back hard. The first hour of this session belonged to the hosts, while the second half was bossed by the Indian spin in tandem, and hence, it will be deemed as a shared session.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get going in the post-lunch session. It has turned cloudy, with the sun now hiding behind the clouds. Akash Deep will start the attack for India. Joe Root to face with Dhruv Jurel up to the stumps. Two slips and a gully in place. Let's play...
... DAY 4, SECOND SESSION ...

The hosts will be eyeing at least another 150 runs from here, and they still have some batting depth to fall back on. As for India, they were disciplined in the morning, and the key will be to stay at the stumps and make the most of the uneven bounce. It was all pace before lunch, but we are likely to see spin introduced after the break. The battle between Stokes and Ravindra Jadeja, especially with the footmarks in play, promises to be a fascinating one. The second session will commence at 6.10 pm IST (12.40 pm GMT). See you then!

Crawley managed to see through that initial burst but couldn’t kick on. As the ball softened, the sharp lift off the deck lessened, but it kept low often enough to plant seeds of doubt in the batters’ minds. Harry Brook looked to play his natural game and put the pressure back on India but with that approach always comes risk, and it eventually caught up with him. England have two of the ideal men for a recovery job. Yes, Ben Stokes may be short on runs, but he spent valuable time out in the middle during the first innings, which would have boosted his confidence. Joe Root, meanwhile, is coming off a century and remains the key.

SESSION SUMMARY - 24 overs, 96 runs and 4 wickets. An entertaining session of Test cricket, one that belonged to India. England landed a punch or two through Harry Brook, but it didn’t last long. After a slow-burning first three days, the surface came to life this morning and how. There was variable bounce, particularly from the Nursery End where Jasprit Bumrah operated, with Zak Crawley taking a few blows on the gloves. But it was Mohammed Siraj who reaped the rewards, picking up a couple of wickets inside the first hour.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. It's all happening out there and has been India's opening hour without a doubt. Lord’s has transformed into an absolute furnace, with intensity running fever pitch. The ball has consistently stayed low and occasionally kicked up from the same deteriorating spots on the pitch, creating a sense of doubt in the batters' minds. A couple of chances have been crafted with edges flying past the cordons and a few audacious strokes thrown in to keep the excitement alive. The dismissals of Duckett and Pope came as a result of relentless bowling pressure from Siraj and Bumrah's opening bursts. And once again, England’s opening stand failed to weather the storm against the new ball and a tiring surface. One thing’s certain, as this contest deepens, mental fortitude will be highly tested for both sides. Joe Root walks in at 4 for England. And Nitish Kumar Reddy has been introduced post the first hydration break. He replaces Jasprit Bumrah.

Commentary.Commentary: Nasser Hussain on-air mentions that once the new ball gets softer, as has been the case in the past as well, the bounce won't be as exaggerated. A brand-new Dukes ball, or any red cherry for that matter, tends to be hard with a pronounced seam, which helps fast bowlers generate extra bounce and movement. But as the ball wears, the seam flattens, and the hardness fades, it comes off the surface more gently. This means batters might find it just a bit easier to deal with deliveries that previously kicked off awkwardly or bounced steeply. Especially on a pitch like Lord’s, where the natural slope and occasional rough spots already create variable bounce, a softer ball reduces that unpredictability by some margin.

PITCH REPORT - Raunak Kapoor reports a cooler and cloudier morning at Lord’s, a stark contrast to the first three days, which were bathed in sunshine and clear blue skies. Informs that it is currently 21 degrees Celsius, with a maximum of 26 degrees Celsius expected later in the day, along with a light breeze across the ground. Deep Dasgupta notes that there hasn’t been much change in terms of wear and tear on the surface. Mentions that ball marks are more visible at the Pavilion End, though they’re mostly on the shorter side and shouldn’t trouble the batters too much. States that there are some footmarks around the left-hander’s off stump at the Nursery End that Ravindra Jadeja could look to exploit. Further says that, as seen every morning so far, there is a decent carry early on, and the heavy roller will likely have an effect for the first 40 minutes or so.

This fourth day holds the key to shaping not just the outcome of the match but perhaps the fate of the series. All results remain in play, and the contest is on a knife’s edge. The ball is fresh, just an over old, and the opening hour will be a stern examination for England’s top order against Bumrah, Akash, and Siraj, each primed to pounce. Buckle up, as the Lord’s prepares for another thriller of a day ahead.

The pitch hasn’t turned that hostile yet, but weariness crept in late on Day 3 with a few keeping low and darting unpredictably. Spin hasn’t had much say so far, though the rough patches might invite a twist in the final stretch. England will be hoping Shoaib Bashir returns fit, but before that, their focus must be on setting a formidable target. A chase of 342 remains the highest ever achieved at Lord’s, while South Africa’s successful 282 in the recent WTC Final will also linger in England’s minds. The situation demanded to switch off Bazball in the first inning, but will they come all guns blazing this time around?

KL Rahul anchored India’s effort with elegance, notching up his second consecutive century at Lord’s and etching his name again on the Honors Board. Yet, the innings never quite broke free, as each time a stand began to flourish, England’s tireless pace trio of Archer, Stokes, and Woakes intervened, maintaining pressure across nearly 120 overs under extreme heat, and keeping India from running away with the contest.

Despite patches of wear and tear, the Lord’s surface held firm for batters willing to apply themselves, rewarding resolve and patience. India capitalised with a string of partnerships that diluted England’s total, as six of the top eight crossed 20, including valuable knocks from Jadeja, Nitish, and Sundar down the order. It mirrored England’s earlier innings, which was also built on steady contributions and important alliances.

The match started at equilibrium, and after nine absorbing and sweat-soaking sessions in the London heat, it has come up to this. 387 vs 387 in the first innings, and it all stands at a stalemate, making this third Test a one-inning shootoff. Any more proof of how closely contested this rivalry has been? In some aspects, we can draw similarities from the Headingley Test. Only six runs separated the two sides in the first innings. But here, for the first time in the series, England will be setting the target and India will be chasing, which, of course, brings more intrigue to the contest.

Hello, everyone! Day 4 dawns in this iconic Lord’s Test in the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy, 2025. There's been a delightful ebb and flow to this match. Just when one side has seemed to take the ascendancy, the other has found a way to punch back. It’s been a stop-start affair, not because of the weather, but due to repeated ball changes with the Dukes losing its firmness and players taking blows that necessitated breaks. Around 7 overs were lost on Day 2, and ten disappeared on Day 3, and seven on the first. And of course, including all the theatre that followed on Saturday evening, which means one whole session was virtually erased. But cricket has been intense and that’s what all want. On that note, welcome to our coverage.

Well then, this draws an extremely entertaining Day 3 of this Lord's Test to a close. After three days of gruelling, seesawing cricket at the Home of Cricket, the scores stand level, with England just a couple of runs in the lead. And what remains now is a one-innings shootout to decide the fate of this riveting Test match and the series ahead. The margins are razor-thin and the Indians will come out inspired by their new-ball stints in this series and pick a couple of quick wickets come Day 4. England's top two will look to see the first challenging hour off with caution and build on their lead. Action on Day 4 begins on Sunday, 13th July and the first ball is scheduled to be bowled at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT). Expect action aplenty. Do join us for the build-up an hour earlier. For now, you can switch the tabs and follow all the live action between England Women and India Women in the 5th and final T20I in Birmingham. But from this matchcenter, it's a goodbye, cheers!

For England, though, the day felt longer than it looked on the scoreboard. With the sun blazing down and sweaty jerseys, their bowlers had to dig deep into their reserves. The absence of Shoaib Bashir, sidelined with a finger injury on his left hand, compounded the challenge. It stripped England of their primary spin option, forcing Joe Root into an extended spell, more out of necessity than tactical nuance. And with all the drama that followed with England coming out to bat, thrown into the spotlight in the dying minutes, managed to navigate the solitary over without any damage. A small win in the larger battle, but one they’ll gladly pocket heading into Day 4.

At 326 for 6, with the deficit still looming, Ravindra Jadeja and Washington Sundar snuffed out any whispers of a collapse. Jadeja went on to raise his third consecutive fifty in this series, anchoring the effort, while Sundar quietly made his presence felt with yet another invaluable lower-order knock. He continues to stretch India’s batting resources in the most crucial phases, and this cameo was no different. But again, as has been the case in this match so far, just when another partnership started to flourish, this time, Chris Woakes came back for a fresh, spirited spell and fished out Jadeja with England drilling into the Indian lower order within 6 overs. Woakes had spring in his steps as he created chances on just about every delivery post Jadeja's dismissal and wrapped India on 387, with scores level.

Ben Stokes, as he so often does, turned the tide just when the partnership between Jadeja and Nitish Kumar Reddy was starting to blossom. A wicket out of nowhere, in early doors of the last session, was followed by a tireless spell brimming with intensity. He surely had the batters dancing to his tune, probing away with every delivery. The pitch, meanwhile, began to show its weariness, with the odd ball deviating unexpectedly, and kicking off a bit of uneven bounce, with the slope playing its role as well. England persisted with Joe Root’s spin from one end, but it barely scratched the surface, save for a couple of testing leaves.

The real tectonic shift came with KL Rahul's dismissal, moments after he brought up his second century at Lord’s. With India still 133 runs behind, panic simmered, mix-ups and jittery calls added spice to an already tense contest. Nitish Kumar Reddy and Ravindra Jadeja then dug in, steadying the ship through England’s inconsistent new-ball spell. Archer bowled with searing pace, but the hosts failed to land decisive blows. Shoaib Bashir’s injury further dented England’s plans as the Dukes began to whisper. The deficit narrowed to 71 by Tea, setting up a mouth-watering final session.

The morning belonged to KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant, who stitched together a resilient 141-run stand to chip away at England’s lead. Rahul was steady, Pant bold and bruised, countering a probing opening spell from Archer and Woakes before finding fluency as the ball softened. England’s constant ball-change appeals and shift to short-ball tactics couldn’t break the rhythm, though Pant did show signs of struggle against the rising deliveries due to his injured left index finger. Just as India seemed set to head into lunch unscathed, a miscommunication led to Pant’s run out, injecting fresh energy into the English camp. This halted the momentum with India still trailing by 139, with the pitch still on a bit on the slower side.
